messages.subject: Smearing procedures and ds function
parts:
Hello,

i have some doubts about smearing data to account for the possible rounding of angles and distances to sigtings, and inclusion of the smearing ranges to the ds function.

Maybe is a dum question but im new to distance sampling and i've been reading about it and still not getting it.

The smear procedure gives me a angle and/or distance ranges, according to the smear parameters. The signing its not a point but an area or intervale where the animal could be, right?!.

My question is how can i include a range of distance values in the ds function if it needs one distance value? Thank you in advance!!

Best regards,

Hugo Parra

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Smearing procedures and ds function
parts:
Hugo

Smearing to deal with rounding is not supported in the ds() function in the Distance R package.

As an alternative, you can specify the cut points of bins into which to place your perpendicular distance data prior to analysis.  The key cut point selection is to place them in such a way as your heaped distances fall near the centre of the bins.  The intention is to specify bins such that they accurately represent where the detected animal may have been (but was inaccurately recorded by the observers).

I hope that answers your question.

After some preliminary runs testing different detection functions using the ds function (via R), the hazard rate function with no adjustments seems to be adequate (lowest AIC) to our line transect data of loggerhead sea turtles sightings collect by observers onboard fishing tuna vessels. The main objective is to include the detection function in dsm, trying to improve model output from our zero inflated data.  

I've attached a figure showing the detection function for the unbinned and binned ( dist.bins<-c(0,2,4,6,8,10,20,30,40,50) ). AIC decreased by 1000 units after binning, which makes me wonder if this significant improvement measured by AIC could be atributted alone by the binning?

Once again, thanks for the valuable help!!

Hugo

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Smearing procedures and ds function
parts:
Hugo

Thanks for sharing the images of your data and detection functions.  Let me correct you on one issue.  You cannot compare models (nor their AIC scores) between binned and unbinned analyses.  You have changed the data themselves in the binning process, hence comparability between AIC values is lost.  The same situation applies with regard to truncation; truncating data changes the data set, thereby negating the ability to make AIC comparisons among truncation distances.

Thank you very much for the prompt reply!!

After some preliminary runs testing different detection functions using the ds function (via R), the hazard rate function with no adjustments seems to be adequate (lowest AIC) to our line transect data of loggerhead sea turtles sightings collect by observers onboard fishing tuna vessels. The main objective is to include the detection function in dsm, trying to improve model output from our zero inflated data.  

I've attached a figure showing the detection function for the unbinned and binned ( dist.bins<-c(0,2,4,6,8,10,20,30,40,50) ). AIC decreased by 1000 units after binning, which makes me wonder if this significant improvement measured by AIC could be atributted alone by the binning?

Once again, thanks for the valuable help!!

Hugo
